# Setup

This notebook scores cached brms fits by approximate leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO) and breaks the result down by type × relation cell.
It is written to work for any cached fit: the four current ones (Gaussian and beta-binomial, games and thermometer) and later ones (a Gaussian with σ by cell, beta-binomial variants with φ by cell, hurdle or inflated custom families).

**LOO is secondary here.** The main model checks are the estimand checks of notebook 3.5 (weighted cell means, raw $AP_t$ and $\Delta AP$, anchor shares). LOO never decides the main model. Its job is a by-cell diagnostic: where a model predicts badly, and whether its predictive distributions are calibrated in each cell.

- Input: the full fits `data/04_models/<fit>.rds` (git-ignored). **Nothing is fitted here.** There is no `brm()` call, and the notebook stops if a fit is missing.
- Cache: every finished chunk of rows is written to `data/04_models/derived/loo/<fit>_<md5>_<mode>_c<chunk size>/` (git-ignored). A stopped run resumes where it stopped.
- Output: `data/05_results/eu25_loo.rds` (pointwise results without person IDs, per-cell summaries, PIT values, a short table for slides).

**Nothing in this notebook is a claim.**

## What Is Compared With What

Each fit is scored on its own scale with its own `log_lik()` (custom families through their `log_lik_*` function). For the Gaussian fits that is a density on the z-scored outcome; for the beta-binomial fits a probability mass on the integers. These two numbers are not on a common scale, so:

- **elpd differences are computed only between fits with the same outcome variable, the same scale and the same rows in the same order.** The code checks the outcome, the country, the person, `der_co` and `der_explicit` row by row and refuses to compute a difference otherwise.
- So a Gaussian against a Gaussian with σ by cell is fine (both z-scale), and a beta-binomial against a distributional, hurdle or inflated beta-binomial is fine (all integer pmfs).
- A Gaussian against a beta-binomial needs the **cross-family module** (`cross_family <- TRUE`). It turns the Gaussian into a pmf on the same integers, $P(Y = y) = \Phi\big((z_{y+1/2} - \mu)/\sigma\big) - \Phi\big((z_{y-1/2} - \mu)/\sigma\big)$, with open bins at the ends of the scale. This is the only valid basis for an elpd difference between a Gaussian and an integer-outcome family. Because both sides are then probabilities of the same integer events, no Jacobian is involved.
- The **LOO-PIT** by cell is scale-free and is the main cross-family by-cell comparison.

## Run Settings

- `run_mode`: `"test"` scores a stratified test set (`test_per_cell` rows per cell) and reports the time per row, from which the full runtime is estimated; `"full"` scores every row.
- `use_subsample`: in full mode, score a stratified subsample of `subsample_per_cell` rows per cell instead of every row (for speed; the smallest cell, games vote-anchored co, has about 2,300 rows). By-cell results are then means over the sampled rows, which is unbiased within a cell because the sample is stratified by cell.
- `cross_family`: also score the Gaussian fits as discretized pmfs (see above).
- `chunk_size`: rows per chunk. PSIS works row by row, so stacking chunks gives exactly the result of one call on all rows.
- All posterior draws are used (4,000 per fit).

```{r}
#| label: setup

# To track render duration
start_time <- Sys.time()

# set width of console output
options(width = 80)


# Install and load required packages
p_required <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "here",
  "brms",
  "cmdstanr",
  "posterior",
  "loo",
  "matrixStats",
  "sessioninfo"
)
packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
p_to_install <- p_required[!(p_required %in% packages)]
if (length(p_to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(p_to_install)
}
sapply(p_required, require, character.only = TRUE)
rm(p_required, p_to_install, packages)

# Run settings
run_mode <- "test"
use_subsample <- FALSE
cross_family <- FALSE
test_per_cell <- 250
subsample_per_cell <- 2000
chunk_size <- 2000
seed <- 2019

loo_fits <- c("games_gauss", "games_bb", "thermo_gauss", "thermo_bb")

model_dir <- here("data", "04_models")
loo_dir <- file.path(model_dir, "derived", "loo")
out_dir <- here("data", "05_results")
dir.create(loo_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

fit_files <- file.path(model_dir, paste0(loo_fits, ".rds"))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(fit_files)))

fit_fingerprint <- function() {
  tibble(
    name = loo_fits,
    md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(fit_files)),
    mtime = file.mtime(fit_files)
  )
}
fp_start <- fit_fingerprint()

mode_tag <- case_when(
  run_mode == "test" ~ paste0("test", test_per_cell),
  use_subsample ~ paste0("sub", subsample_per_cell),
  TRUE ~ "full"
)
mode_tag
```

# Data

The estimation data are rebuilt exactly as in notebooks 3.3 and 3.5 (copied from 3.2). **This code must stay identical to 3.2.**
The LOO cell is type × relation in the thermometer, and type × relation × game in the games.

```{r}
#| label: data

eu25_games <- read_rds(here("data", "03_final", "eu25_games.rds"))
eu25_thermo <- read_rds(here("data", "03_final", "eu25_thermo.rds"))

# Games, as in 3.2 (games-sample)
games <- eu25_games |>
  filter(
    type %in% c("explicit", "vote_anchored"),
    der_cj_partisan_relationship %in% c("co", "out")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    der_explicit = as.integer(type == "explicit"),
    der_co = as.integer(der_cj_partisan_relationship == "co"),
    der_trust = as.integer(game == "trust"),
    der_wave3 = as.integer(wave == 3),
    der_cell = paste(type, der_cj_partisan_relationship),
    der_anchor = paste(country, anchor, sep = ": "),
    round = factor(round),
    across(c(cj_age, cj_sex, cj_rel, cj_class, der_cj_eu_identity), factor)
  ) |>
  mutate(der_w = 1 / n(), .by = meta_responseid)

games_scale <- list(mean = mean(games$cj_pl2), sd = sd(games$cj_pl2))
games <- games |>
  mutate(der_y_z = (cj_pl2 - games_scale$mean) / games_scale$sd)

# Thermometer, as in 3.2 (thermo-sample)
thermo <- eu25_thermo |>
  filter(
    type %in% c("explicit", "vote_anchored"),
    der_thermo_relationship %in% c("co", "out")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    der_explicit = as.integer(type == "explicit"),
    der_co = as.integer(der_thermo_relationship == "co"),
    der_wave3 = as.integer(wave == 3),
    der_cell = paste(type, der_thermo_relationship),
    der_anchor = paste(country, anchor, sep = ": ")
  ) |>
  mutate(der_w = 1 / n(), .by = meta_responseid)

thermo_scale <- list(mean = mean(thermo$q_thermo), sd = sd(thermo$q_thermo))
thermo <- thermo |>
  mutate(der_y_z = (q_thermo - thermo_scale$mean) / thermo_scale$sd)

# LOO cells
games <- mutate(games, der_cell_loo = paste(der_cell, game))
thermo <- mutate(thermo, der_cell_loo = der_cell)

datasets <- list(games = games, thermo = thermo)
scales <- list(games = games_scale, thermo = thermo_scale)
```

# LOO Code

## Fit Descriptions and the Comparability Rule

Every scored object carries its outcome variable, its scale and its row keys.
`compare_ok()` is the only gate to `elpd_diff_cells()`.

```{r}
#| label: spec-code

specs <- tibble(name = loo_fits) |>
  mutate(
    measure = sub("_.*", "", name),
    family = if_else(grepl("gauss", name), "gaussian", "beta_binomial"),
    yvar = case_when(
      family == "gaussian" ~ "der_y_z",
      measure == "games" ~ "cj_pl2",
      TRUE ~ "q_thermo"
    ),
    # Scale of the scored density: z (continuous) or the integer pmf
    scale = if_else(family == "gaussian", "z", "integer"),
    top = if_else(measure == "games", 10, 100)
  )

# Row keys: the outcome on its native integer scale and the design identifiers
row_keys <- function(fd, measure, yvar) {
  sc <- scales[[measure]]
  y <- if (yvar == "der_y_z") fd[[yvar]] * sc$sd + sc$mean else fd[[yvar]]
  tibble(
    y = as.integer(round(y)),
    country = as.character(fd$country),
    meta_pid = as.character(fd$meta_pid),
    der_co = as.integer(fd$der_co),
    der_explicit = as.integer(fd$der_explicit)
  )
}

compare_ok <- function(a, b) {
  same_outcome <- identical(a$outcome, b$outcome) && identical(a$scale, b$scale)
  same_rows <- identical(a$rows, b$rows) && identical(a$keys, b$keys)
  if (!same_outcome) {
    message(a$label, " vs ", b$label, ": different outcome or scale (",
      a$outcome, "/", a$scale, " vs ", b$outcome, "/", b$scale, ")")
  }
  if (!same_rows) message(a$label, " vs ", b$label, ": different rows")
  same_outcome && same_rows
}

# Pointwise elpd differences, overall and by cell; refuses non-comparable pairs
elpd_diff_cells <- function(a, b) {
  if (!compare_ok(a, b)) stop("elpd difference refused: fits are not comparable")
  d <- tibble(cell = a$cell, diff = a$elpd - b$elpd)
  bind_rows(
    summarise(d, cell = "all", n = n(), elpd_diff = sum(diff), se = sqrt(n * var(diff))),
    summarise(d, n = n(), elpd_diff = sum(diff), se = sqrt(n * var(diff)), .by = cell)
  ) |>
    mutate(a = a$label, b = b$label, .before = 1)
}
```

## Rows to Score

```{r}
#| label: rows-code

stratified_rows <- function(d, n_per) {
  set.seed(seed)
  idx <- split(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$der_cell_loo)
  sort(unlist(
    lapply(idx, \(i) if (length(i) <= n_per) i else sample(i, n_per)),
    use.names = FALSE
  ))
}

rows_to_score <- function(d) {
  if (run_mode == "test") return(stratified_rows(d, test_per_cell))
  if (use_subsample) return(stratified_rows(d, subsample_per_cell))
  seq_len(nrow(d))
}
```

## One Chunk

For a chunk of rows, all with all 4,000 draws:

1. `log_lik()`: the pointwise log predictive density of each draw.
2. PSIS (`loo::psis()` with relative efficiencies by chain) gives the smoothed, normalized log importance weights $\log w_{is}$ and the Pareto $\hat{k}$ of each row. The LOO log predictive density of row $i$ is $\log \sum_s w_{is}\, p(y_i \mid \theta_s)$.
3. LOO-PIT, with the same weights and the replicated outcomes of `posterior_predict()` for the same rows and draws. For integer outcomes the randomized PIT $u_i = P_{\text{loo}}(Y < y_i) + V_i\, P_{\text{loo}}(Y = y_i)$ with $V_i \sim U(0, 1)$, which is uniform under a calibrated model; for the Gaussian on the z-scale the plain $u_i = P_{\text{loo}}(Y \le y_i)$.

The random numbers (replications and $V_i$) are seeded per chunk, so a resumed run gives the same values as an uninterrupted one.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-code

psis_elpd <- function(ll, chains) {
  r_eff <- loo::relative_eff(exp(ll), chain_id = chains)
  ps <- suppressWarnings(loo::psis(-ll, r_eff = r_eff))
  lw <- weights(ps, log = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)
  list(elpd = colLogSumExps(lw + ll), k = ps$diagnostics$pareto_k, lw = lw)
}

loo_chunk <- function(fit, nd, yvar, gauss, chunk_id) {
  set.seed(seed + chunk_id)
  chains <- rep(seq_len(nchains(fit)), each = ndraws(fit) / nchains(fit))
  ll <- log_lik(fit, newdata = nd)
  p <- psis_elpd(ll, chains)
  rm(ll)

  yrep <- posterior_predict(fit, newdata = nd)
  y <- nd[[yvar]]
  ymat <- matrix(y, nrow(yrep), ncol(yrep), byrow = TRUE)
  w <- exp(p$lw)
  pit <- if (gauss) {
    colSums(w * (yrep <= ymat))
  } else {
    colSums(w * (yrep < ymat)) + runif(length(y)) * colSums(w * (yrep == ymat))
  }
  tibble(elpd = p$elpd, k = p$k, pit = pmin(pmax(pit, 0), 1))
}
```

## Cross-Family Module (optional)

Only run with `cross_family <- TRUE`, and only for Gaussian fits.
`log_bin()` is the log probability of the integer bin of $y$ under $N(\mu, \sigma)$ on the z-scale, computed on the log scale in the tail that is numerically stable.
The discretization check confirms, on the first chunk, that the bin probabilities of a row sum to 1 over the whole scale, and compares the binned log probability with the continuous density approximation $\log \phi(z_i; \mu, \sigma) - \log(\text{SD}_y)$ for interior values. The two should be close where the bin is narrow relative to $\sigma$.

```{r}
#| label: cross-family-code

# log P(lo < Z < hi) for Z ~ N(mu, sigma); mu: draws x rows, sigma: draws
log_bin <- function(mu, sigma, lo, hi) {
  a <- sweep(-mu, 2, lo, "+") / sigma
  b <- sweep(-mu, 2, hi, "+") / sigma
  lower <- {
    lb <- pnorm(b, log.p = TRUE)
    lb + log1p(-exp(pnorm(a, log.p = TRUE) - lb))
  }
  upper <- {
    ua <- pnorm(a, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
    ua + log1p(-exp(pnorm(b, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE) - ua))
  }
  ifelse(a > 0, upper, lower)
}

bin_edges <- function(y, sc, top) {
  list(
    lo = ifelse(y == 0, -Inf, (y - 0.5 - sc$mean) / sc$sd),
    hi = ifelse(y == top, Inf, (y + 0.5 - sc$mean) / sc$sd)
  )
}

bin_chunk <- function(fit, nd, sc, top, check = FALSE) {
  chains <- rep(seq_len(nchains(fit)), each = ndraws(fit) / nchains(fit))
  mu <- posterior_epred(fit, newdata = nd)
  sigma <- as_draws_df(fit, variable = "sigma")$sigma
  yn <- round(nd$der_y_z * sc$sd + sc$mean)
  stopifnot(all(abs(nd$der_y_z * sc$sd + sc$mean - yn) < 1e-8))
  e <- bin_edges(yn, sc, top)
  ll <- log_bin(mu, sigma, e$lo, e$hi)
  p <- psis_elpd(ll, chains)

  chk <- NULL
  if (check) {
    # Bin probabilities over the whole scale sum to 1 (first 20 rows, 50 draws)
    s <- seq_len(min(50, nrow(mu)))
    sums <- sapply(seq_len(min(20, ncol(mu))), \(i) {
      ek <- bin_edges(0:top, sc, top)
      p_k <- sapply(0:top, \(k) exp(log_bin(
        mu[s, rep(i, 1), drop = FALSE], sigma[s], ek$lo[k + 1], ek$hi[k + 1]
      )))
      range(rowSums(p_k))
    })
    interior <- yn > 0 & yn < top
    ll_cont <- dnorm(
      matrix(nd$der_y_z, nrow(mu), ncol(mu), byrow = TRUE), mu, sigma, log = TRUE
    ) - log(sc$sd)
    chk <- tibble(
      max_abs_sum_minus_1 = max(abs(sums - 1)),
      median_abs_diff_interior = median(abs(ll - ll_cont)[, interior]),
      p90_abs_diff_interior = quantile(abs(ll - ll_cont)[, interior], 0.9)
    )
  }
  list(res = tibble(elpd_bin = p$elpd, k_bin = p$k), check = chk)
}
```

## Resumable Driver

`score_fit()` loads one fit, checks its rows against the rebuilt data, and scores the selected rows chunk by chunk.
A chunk that already has a file is skipped. Each chunk file holds its row indices, the results and the seconds it took.

```{r}
#| label: driver-code

score_fit <- function(spec) {
  d <- datasets[[spec$measure]]
  rows <- rows_to_score(d)
  md5 <- fp_start$md5[fp_start$name == spec$name]
  dir <- file.path(
    loo_dir,
    paste0(spec$name, "_", substr(md5, 1, 8), "_", mode_tag, "_c", chunk_size)
  )
  dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  chunks <- split(rows, ceiling(seq_along(rows) / chunk_size))
  gauss <- spec$family == "gaussian"
  sc <- scales[[spec$measure]]

  todo_native <- !file.exists(file.path(dir, sprintf("chunk_%04d.rds", seq_along(chunks))))
  todo_bin <- cross_family & gauss &
    !file.exists(file.path(dir, sprintf("chunk_%04d_bin.rds", seq_along(chunks))))

  fit <- NULL
  if (any(todo_native | todo_bin)) {
    fit <- read_rds(file.path(model_dir, paste0(spec$name, ".rds")))
    fd <- fit$data
    stopifnot(
      nrow(fd) == nrow(d),
      identical(row_keys(fd, spec$measure, spec$yvar), row_keys(d, spec$measure, spec$yvar))
    )
  }

  for (j in seq_along(chunks)) {
    nd <- d[chunks[[j]], ]
    if (todo_native[j]) {
      t0 <- Sys.time()
      res <- loo_chunk(fit, nd, spec$yvar, gauss, j)
      secs <- as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")
      write_rds(list(rows = chunks[[j]], res = res, secs = secs),
        file.path(dir, sprintf("chunk_%04d.rds", j)))
      message(spec$name, " chunk ", j, "/", length(chunks), ": ", round(secs), " s")
    }
    if (todo_bin[j]) {
      t0 <- Sys.time()
      b <- bin_chunk(fit, nd, sc, spec$top, check = (j == 1))
      secs <- as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")
      write_rds(list(rows = chunks[[j]], res = b$res, check = b$check, secs = secs),
        file.path(dir, sprintf("chunk_%04d_bin.rds", j)))
      message(spec$name, " bin chunk ", j, "/", length(chunks), ": ", round(secs), " s")
    }
  }
  rm(fit)
  gc()

  # Collect
  read_chunks <- function(suffix) {
    f <- file.path(dir, sprintf("chunk_%04d%s.rds", seq_along(chunks), suffix))
    parts <- map(f, read_rds)
    stopifnot(identical(unlist(map(parts, "rows")), rows))
    list(
      res = bind_rows(map(parts, "res")),
      secs = sum(map_dbl(parts, "secs")),
      check = bind_rows(map(parts, "check"))
    )
  }
  native <- read_chunks("")
  bin <- if (cross_family && gauss) read_chunks("_bin") else NULL

  list(
    spec = spec,
    rows = rows,
    keys = row_keys(d[rows, ], spec$measure, spec$yvar),
    native = native,
    bin = bin
  )
}
```

# Scoring

The fits are scored one at a time; each is dropped from memory before the next is loaded.

```{r}
#| label: score

scored <- map(seq_len(nrow(specs)), \(i) score_fit(as.list(specs[i, ])))
names(scored) <- specs$name
```

## Runtime

Seconds per row, and the runtime a full run would need (all rows, all draws, one fit after the other).
In test mode, this is the estimate to check before switching to `run_mode <- "full"`.

```{r}
#| label: runtime

runtime <- imap(scored, \(s, nm) {
  n_full <- nrow(datasets[[s$spec$measure]])
  tibble(
    name = nm,
    rows_scored = length(s$rows),
    secs = s$native$secs + if (is.null(s$bin)) 0 else s$bin$secs,
    secs_per_row = secs / rows_scored,
    rows_full = n_full,
    est_full_hours = secs_per_row * n_full / 3600
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()

bind_rows(runtime, summarise(runtime, name = "total", est_full_hours = sum(est_full_hours))) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 4, 0, 1))
```

# Pointwise Results

One row per scored data row and fit: the cell, the LOO elpd, Pareto $\hat{k}$, the LOO-PIT value and, for integer-outcome scores, the leave-one-out empirical baseline.

**The baseline.** Each row is predicted by the frequencies of the *other* rows in its cell, smoothed with +0.5 per scale value: $p_i = (n_{c, y_i} - 1 + 0.5) / (N_c - 1 + 0.5 K)$, with $K = 11$ or $101$ scale values. The model's elpd per row minus this baseline shows how much the model gains over the raw cell distribution. It exists only for integer pmfs: the beta-binomial fits, and the Gaussian fits when scored through the cross-family module.

```{r}
#| label: pointwise

baseline_ll <- function(d, measure, top) {
  y <- if (measure == "games") d$cj_pl2 else d$q_thermo
  n_cell <- ave(y, d$der_cell_loo, FUN = length)
  n_val <- ave(y, d$der_cell_loo, y, FUN = length)
  log((n_val - 1 + 0.5) / (n_cell - 1 + 0.5 * (top + 1)))
}

pointwise <- imap(scored, \(s, nm) {
  d <- datasets[[s$spec$measure]]
  base <- baseline_ll(d, s$spec$measure, s$spec$top)[s$rows]
  out <- tibble(
    name = nm,
    measure = s$spec$measure,
    family = s$spec$family,
    row = s$rows,
    der_cell = d$der_cell[s$rows],
    cell = d$der_cell_loo[s$rows],
    game = if (s$spec$measure == "games") d$game[s$rows] else NA_character_,
    country = d$country[s$rows],
    y = s$keys$y,
    elpd = s$native$res$elpd,
    k = s$native$res$k,
    pit = s$native$res$pit,
    baseline = base,
    elpd_bin = if (is.null(s$bin)) NA_real_ else s$bin$res$elpd_bin,
    k_bin = if (is.null(s$bin)) NA_real_ else s$bin$res$k_bin
  )
  # The baseline gain is defined for integer pmfs only
  mutate(
    out,
    gain_native = if (s$spec$family == "gaussian") NA_real_ else elpd - baseline,
    gain_bin = elpd_bin - baseline
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()
```

# Per-Cell Diagnostics

## 1. elpd per Row and Pareto k̂

The mean LOO elpd per row in each cell, with its standard error, and the share of rows with $\hat{k} > 0.7$ and $\hat{k} > 1$.

**How to read it.** Within one model, the elpd per row mixes two things: how spread out the outcome is in that cell, and how badly the model fits there. A cell with widely spread ratings has a low elpd per row even under a perfect model. So this shows where a model predicts with least certainty, not on its own where it fits worst. It is comparable across fits only within a comparable set (section 4).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-elpd-cell

cell_summary <- function(df, ...) {
  df |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      elpd_mean = mean(elpd),
      elpd_se = sd(elpd) / sqrt(n),
      share_k_07 = mean(k > 0.7),
      share_k_1 = mean(k > 1),
      .by = c(...)
    )
}

elpd_cell <- bind_rows(
  cell_summary(pointwise, name, der_cell) |> rename(cell = der_cell),
  cell_summary(filter(pointwise, measure == "games"), name, cell)
) |>
  distinct()

elpd_cell |>
  arrange(name, cell) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Reliability

Shares of rows with $\hat{k} > 0.7$ (PSIS estimate unreliable) and $\hat{k} > 1$ (unusable), by fit.
The by-cell table is repeated on the rows with $\hat{k} \le 0.7$ as a check. These rows are **not** a random subset: high $\hat{k}$ marks influential rows, which are often the poorly predicted ones, so the restricted results flatter the model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reliability

pointwise |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    share_k_07 = mean(k > 0.7),
    share_k_1 = mean(k > 1),
    max_k = max(k),
    .by = name
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

cell_summary(filter(pointwise, k <= 0.7), name, der_cell) |>
  arrange(name, der_cell) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Leave-one-out here leaves out **one row**, not one person. A person contributes several rounds or ratings, and the person intercept learns from the other rows of the same person, so row-level LOO is optimistic about predicting a new person.
Leave-one-person-out would need either K-fold cross-validation grouped by `meta_pid` (which means refits) or PSIS with moment matching, which needs fits saved with `save_pars(all = TRUE)`. Neither is done here. The current fits predate `save_pars(all = TRUE)`, and new fits from notebook 3.2 keep all parameters.

## 2. LOO-PIT by Cell

Under a calibrated model the LOO-PIT values are uniform in every cell.
The figure shows the difference between their empirical CDF and the uniform CDF, with a pointwise 95% band for a uniform sample of that size.
A hump above zero in the lower half means too many observations fall in the lower tail of the predictive distribution, for example more zeros than the model expects.
Because the PIT is scale-free, it compares fits across families directly.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pit
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

pit_grid <- seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01)
pit_ecdf <- pointwise |>
  reframe(
    u = pit_grid,
    ecdf_diff = ecdf(pit)(pit_grid) - pit_grid,
    band = 1.96 * sqrt(pit_grid * (1 - pit_grid) / n()),
    .by = c(name, measure, family, der_cell)
  )

ggplot(pit_ecdf, aes(x = u)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = -band, ymax = band), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(aes(y = ecdf_diff, colour = family), linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(measure ~ der_cell) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(gaussian = "#08306b", beta_binomial = "#d94801")) +
  labs(
    title = "LOO-PIT: empirical CDF minus uniform CDF, by cell",
    subtitle = "Grey: pointwise 95% band for a uniform sample of the same size",
    x = "u",
    y = "ECDF(u) - u",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pit

pit_cell <- pointwise |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    share_pit_below_05 = mean(pit < 0.05),
    share_pit_above_95 = mean(pit > 0.95),
    max_abs_ecdf_diff = max(abs(ecdf(pit)(pit_grid) - pit_grid)),
    .by = c(name, der_cell)
  )
pit_cell |>
  arrange(name, der_cell) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## 3. Gain over the Empirical Cell Distribution

For integer pmfs only: the mean of model elpd minus baseline per row, by cell.
Positive values mean the model predicts a row better than the raw distribution of its cell does.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gain

gain_cell <- bind_rows(
  pointwise |>
    filter(!is.na(gain_native)) |>
    summarise(n = n(), gain_mean = mean(gain_native), gain_se = sd(gain_native) / sqrt(n),
      .by = c(name, der_cell)) |>
    mutate(score = "native"),
  pointwise |>
    filter(!is.na(gain_bin)) |>
    summarise(n = n(), gain_mean = mean(gain_bin), gain_se = sd(gain_bin) / sqrt(n),
      .by = c(name, der_cell)) |>
    mutate(score = "discretized")
)

gain_cell |>
  arrange(name, score, der_cell) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## 4. elpd Differences within Comparable Sets

The scored objects are the native scores of every fit and, with `cross_family <- TRUE`, the discretized scores of the Gaussian fits.
Every pair with the same outcome, scale and rows is compared; every other pair is refused by `compare_ok()`.
The standard error of a summed difference over $N$ rows is $\sqrt{N \cdot \text{var}(d_i)}$.

```{r}
#| label: comparisons

scores <- list()
for (nm in names(scored)) {
  s <- scored[[nm]]
  pw <- filter(pointwise, name == nm)
  scores[[nm]] <- list(
    label = nm,
    outcome = sub("_.*", "", nm),
    scale = s$spec$scale,
    rows = s$rows,
    keys = s$keys,
    cell = pw$der_cell,
    elpd = pw$elpd
  )
  if (!is.null(s$bin)) {
    scores[[paste0(nm, "_bin")]] <- list(
      label = paste0(nm, " (discretized)"),
      outcome = sub("_.*", "", nm),
      scale = "integer",
      rows = s$rows,
      keys = s$keys,
      cell = pw$der_cell,
      elpd = pw$elpd_bin
    )
  }
}

pairs <- combn(names(scores), 2, simplify = FALSE)
comparable <- keep(pairs, \(p) {
  a <- scores[[p[1]]]
  b <- scores[[p[2]]]
  identical(a$outcome, b$outcome) && identical(a$scale, b$scale)
})

elpd_diffs <- if (length(comparable)) {
  map(comparable, \(p) elpd_diff_cells(scores[[p[1]]], scores[[p[2]]])) |> bind_rows()
} else {
  message("No comparable pair among the scored fits (set cross_family <- TRUE to compare Gaussian and beta-binomial).")
  NULL
}

# The gate refuses a non-comparable pair
refused <- tryCatch(
  {
    elpd_diff_cells(scores[["games_gauss"]], scores[["games_bb"]])
    FALSE
  },
  error = \(e) TRUE
)
stopifnot(refused)

if (!is.null(elpd_diffs)) knitr::kable(elpd_diffs, digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: discretization-check

disc_check <- imap(scored, \(s, nm) {
  if (is.null(s$bin)) return(NULL)
  mutate(s$bin$check, name = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  bind_rows()
if (nrow(disc_check)) knitr::kable(disc_check, digits = 4)
```

# Save

```{r}
#| label: save

slide_table <- elpd_cell |>
  filter(cell %in% unique(pointwise$der_cell)) |>
  left_join(
    select(pit_cell, name, cell = der_cell, max_abs_ecdf_diff),
    by = c("name", "cell")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    gain_cell |>
      filter(score == "native" | grepl("gauss", name)) |>
      select(name, cell = der_cell, gain_mean),
    by = c("name", "cell")
  ) |>
  select(name, cell, n, elpd_mean, share_k_07, max_abs_ecdf_diff, gain_mean)

write_rds(
  list(
    settings = list(
      run_mode = run_mode, mode_tag = mode_tag, cross_family = cross_family,
      chunk_size = chunk_size, seed = seed
    ),
    pointwise = pointwise,
    elpd_cell = elpd_cell,
    pit_cell = pit_cell,
    pit_ecdf = pit_ecdf,
    gain_cell = gain_cell,
    elpd_diffs = elpd_diffs,
    disc_check = disc_check,
    runtime = runtime,
    slide_table = slide_table
  ),
  file.path(out_dir, "eu25_loo.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
file.size(file.path(out_dir, "eu25_loo.rds")) / 1e6
```
